title: Rumi on Pain and Healing: The Cure Hidden in the Wound
subtitle: Eight Persian Sufi poems with English translation
yt_title: Rumi on Pain and Healing | 8 Persian Sufi Poems with English Translation
intro: Rumi never promised a life without pain.
What he offered was another way of looking at it: pain as a door, longing as a medicine.
Here are eight passages about pain and the healing that comes through it.

poems.name: The Pain That Is Our Cure

lines.fa: درد شمس الدین بود سرمایه درمان ما
lines.en: The pain of Shams al-Din is the capital of our cure;

lines.fa: بی سر و سامانی عشقش بود سامان ما
lines.en: the homelessness of his love is our home and order.

tafsir: Shams of Tabriz turned Rumi's life upside down, and then disappeared.
That was painful. Rumi does not deny it.
But he says the pain itself became his wealth, the capital from which healing grew.
Some wounds are where the medicine enters.

poems.name: From Dream to Union

lines.fa: هر چه بر اصحاب حال باشد اول خیال
lines.en: Whatever comes to the people of the heart first as imagination

lines.fa: گردد آخر وصال چونک درآید نگار
lines.en: becomes union at last, when the Beloved walks in.

tafsir: At first, what we long for is only a picture in the mind.
We imagine healing, we imagine love, and it feels unreal.
Rumi says: wait. One day the Beloved walks through the door.
The longing was not foolish. It was the first shape of what was coming.

poems.name: The Nightingale

lines.en: The poor nightingale, what it suffers!

lines.fa: آه از آن گل که چه‌ها می‌کند
lines.en: Ah, that rose, the things it does!

tafsir: The nightingale loves the rose and sings all night in pain.
Rumi sighs over both of them.
The rose causes the pain, and the rose is also the reason for the song.
What hurts us most is often bound up with what we love most.

poems.name: You Are the Water of Life

lines.en: O you whose union is the water of life,
you know the way to set us free.

lines.fa: از دیده برون مشو که نوری
lines.en: Do not leave my eyes, for you are light;

lines.fa: وز سینه جدا مشو که جانی
lines.en: do not part from my chest, for you are soul.

tafsir: Here Rumi prays to the Beloved directly.
You know how to free us, he says. We do not.
Healing is not a technique he masters. It is a presence he asks to stay.
Stay in my eyes. Stay in my chest. That is the whole prayer.

poems.name: Not Fallen From My Hand

lines.fa: اگر فانی شود عالم ز دریایی بود شبنم
lines.en: If the world passes away, it is only a dewdrop from an ocean;

lines.fa: گر افتاده‌ست او از خود نیفتاده‌ست از دستم
lines.en: if it has fallen from itself, it has not fallen from My hand.

tafsir: The voice here is the Beloved's.
Everything we lose is like a dewdrop. The ocean it came from remains.
And even what falls apart has not fallen out of God's hand.
In the middle of loss, Rumi offers this: nothing is truly dropped.

poems.name: Make This World See That World

lines.fa: ای دو چشم جهان به تو روشن
lines.en: O you by whom both eyes of the world are bright,

lines.fa: این جهان را تو آن جهان بین کن
lines.en: make this world able to see that world.

tafsir: Rumi asks for a healing of sight.
Not another world, but new eyes in this one.
So that here, in ordinary life, we can glimpse what lies beyond it.
Often that is what healing means: seeing differently.

poems.name: His Breath Gives Life

lines.fa: با دم او می‌رود عین الحیات
lines.en: With his breath flows the spring of life;

lines.fa: مرده جان یابد چو او تلقین کند
lines.en: the dead find a soul when he whispers to them.

tafsir: Jesus, in Persian poetry, heals with his breath.
Rumi gives that power to the Beloved.
One breath, one whispered word, and what was dead comes alive.
We have all known someone whose words brought us back to life.

poems.name: Pearl of the Heart's Sea

lines.fa: ای گوهر دریای دل چه جای جان چه جای دل
lines.en: O pearl of the heart's ocean, what is soul, what is heart, beside you?

lines.fa: روشن ز تو شب‌های دل خرم ز تو ایام دل
lines.en: By you the heart's nights are bright; by you its days are glad.

tafsir: We end with gratitude.
The heart has nights and days, dark seasons and bright ones.
Rumi says the Beloved lights both.
Healing does not mean there are no more nights. It means even the nights have light.
